name: Landmark Group
why: Current employer. The UAE head office runs the group FP&A his Malaysia seat reports into — an internal move is the shortest path to a controller title he has.
watch: Internal mobility is read as a lateral unless he arrives with a mandate. Fix that by applying to a named UAE vacancy, not by asking for a transfer.

name: Al-Futtaim
why: The closest structural twin to Landmark: multi-vertical, multi-entity, IFRS group reporting, and a standing FP&A manager population at exactly his grade. His feed has seen 26 postings.
watch: Volume of applicants. The portal is a queue; a referral or a retained agency is what moves a CV out of it.

name: Majid Al Futtaim
why: Carrefour franchise plus mall and leisure P&Ls — the retail-plus-property mix is his exact reading. Posts commercial finance roles continuously.
watch: Hires heavily from within and from Big 4 Dubai. Arrive via the audit-alumni route if there is one.

name: Chalhoub Group
why: Luxury distribution and own-retail: principal-vs-agent revenue judgement under IFRS 15 is the technical centre of the job, which is the argument he can make better than most.
watch: Luxury wants luxury on the CV. Lead with the distribution economics, not the brand names.

name: GMG
why: Multi-brand franchise retail with factory and distribution arms. Already posting senior finance roles his feed captured.
watch: Smaller finance function than the top three — fewer seats, so timing matters more than fit.

name: Apparel Group
why: Indian-promoted, Indian-CA-dense finance function running 85+ brands across the GCC. Structurally the most receptive employer on this list to his exact profile.
watch: Pay bands sit below Al-Futtaim and MAF for the same title. Worth it as a title step, not as a pay step.

name: Al Tayer Group
why: Retail plus automotive plus hospitality under one group — the breadth his Landmark experience maps onto without translation.
watch: Conservative, slow hiring cycle. Treat as a six-month pipeline, not a live application.

name: Alshaya Group
why: The largest franchise operator in the region — Starbucks, H&M, Mothercare. Franchise-fee and royalty accounting is adjacent to what he already reports.
watch: Kuwait-headquartered, so the strongest seats are in Kuwait rather than Dubai. Confirm the posting's actual location.

name: Lulu Group International
why: Indian-owned, Indian-CA-run finance function at genuine scale across the GCC and India. Hires at controller grade routinely.
watch: Known for long hours and a lean finance structure relative to revenue. Ask about span of control early.

name: Americana Restaurants
why: ADX and Tadawul listed QSR operator — listed-company reporting discipline plus unit-economics FP&A, which is the combination that reads best for a Head of FP&A title.
watch: Listed means a defined FP&A ladder and internal candidates for every rung.

name: Emaar Properties
why: Listed developer with malls, hospitality and retail. Property revenue recognition is a learnable adjacency rather than a different trade.
watch: Development accounting (cost-to-complete, percentage of completion) is a real knowledge gap he has to close before interview, not during.

name: Aldar Properties
why: ADX-listed, Abu Dhabi. His feed has already captured seven postings including AVP-grade finance seats — the highest hard-evidence signal outside his own employer.
watch: Abu Dhabi, not Dubai: a relocation decision, and an Emiratisation-dense market.

name: Damac Properties
why: High-volume residential developer with a large transaction-processing finance function that needs controllers.
watch: Cyclical hiring and a reputation for churn in finance. Check tenure of the last two holders of the seat.

name: Sobha Realty
why: Indian-promoted developer; finance leadership is predominantly Indian CA. Receptive to his credential without translation.
watch: Single-asset-class exposure — a narrowing move if he stays more than three years.

name: Nakheel
why: Government-related developer with retail and leisure assets. Scale guarantees the seat exists.
watch: Government-related entity: slower process, and more weight on UAE experience than on sector fit.

name: Dubai Holding
why: Holding structure with hotels, malls and retail — group consolidation at a scale where IAS 21 and intercompany elimination are the daily job.
watch: Hires senior finance largely from within the Dubai Inc. ecosystem. Hard to enter cold.

name: Jumeirah Group
why: Hotel P&Ls: RevPAR, ADR and GOP are the metrics he would own, and the hospitality dialect he has from the group's Malaysian F&B exposure.
watch: Hotel finance careers often run through property-level controller roles first. Expect a step sideways before up.

name: Rotana Hotel Management
why: The largest homegrown regional hotel operator — many property controller seats and a real corporate FP&A function above them.
watch: Property-level roles are the volume; the corporate seats are few and rarely advertised.

name: Minor Hotels / Anantara ME
why: His feed captured a finance manager posting directly. Asia-Pacific parentage makes his Malaysia tenure an asset rather than a detour.
watch: Smaller regional finance team; the controller seat may be single-property rather than cluster.

name: Accor Middle East
why: Cluster-controller model across Rixos, Sofitel, Novotel and ibis — and he has an ibis Malaysia posting in his own feed, which proves the group hires in both his markets.
watch: Matrixed reporting into Paris and into the owner. Two masters per P&L.

name: Marriott International MEA
why: Largest hotel platform in the region; standardised finance ladder means the next rung is defined rather than negotiated.
watch: US-listed process rigour and a strong internal-promotion norm. Entry is usually at property level.

name: IHG Hotels & Resorts MEA
why: Already in his feed with a Dubai business-support manager role — hard evidence of hiring at his grade.
watch: Owner-operator split means the seat's real authority varies property to property. Ask who signs the capex.

name: Hilton MEA
why: Regional cluster finance across a large managed estate.
watch: Same property-first entry pattern as Marriott.

name: Kerzner International
why: Atlantis and One&Only: small number of very large single-asset P&Ls, so the controller seat carries unusual weight.
watch: Very few seats. Opportunistic only.

name: Emirates Group
why: Owns dnata, hotels and retail alongside the airline — a group FP&A function large enough to have many entry points.
watch: Aviation finance is its own technical dialect, and internal candidates are plentiful.

name: Etihad Airways
why: Ten postings in his feed including cost-management seats. Proof of volume hiring, if not of sector fit.
watch: Airline cost accounting and fleet economics are a genuine gap. The fit score the feed gave (54) is honest.

name: DP World
why: Global logistics group with heavy multi-currency consolidation — the IAS 21 half of his experience transfers cleanly.
watch: Asset-heavy infrastructure finance, not retail unit economics. Expect to be outbid by logistics-native candidates.

name: Aramex
why: Listed, multi-country, franchise and owned-station mix. Principal-vs-agent again — the same IFRS 15 argument as luxury distribution.
watch: Margin pressure in the sector has meant repeated cost programmes. Ask what happened to the last incumbent.

name: Agthia Group
why: ADX-listed food and beverage with an acquisition programme — purchase accounting and integration FP&A is a real growth brief.
watch: Manufacturing cost accounting is more standard-costing than retail gross-margin work.

name: IFFCO Group
why: Indian-promoted FMCG group; his feed captured a corporate finance manager posting. Indian-CA-dense finance leadership.
watch: Privately held, so limited published financials to prepare from. Ask for segment structure in the first call.

name: Al Ghurair Investment
why: Family conglomerate of exactly the type that appoints Indian CAs to controller seats and keeps them for a decade.
watch: Family governance: the real decision sits with the owner, not the CFO. Longer, more relational process.

name: Easa Saleh Al Gurg Group
why: Multi-business family group with retail and distribution arms. High receptivity to his credential.
watch: Smaller FP&A function; the role may be controller-plus-everything rather than specialised.

name: Al Khayyat Investments
why: Distribution plus own-retail plus healthcare — three P&L shapes he has seen in one group.
watch: Lower public profile means less to research. Expect to ask most questions live.

name: AW Rostamani Group
why: Diversified family group with retail and property arms.
watch: Automotive is the core; retail and property are the periphery where the smaller seats are.

name: Juma Al Majid Group
why: Large distribution group, Indian-CA-dense, hires at controller grade.
watch: Very low digital hiring footprint. Agency or referral only, realistically.

name: Galadari Brothers
why: Franchise F&B plus distribution — the franchise-fee accounting adjacency again.
watch: Small corporate finance team; the seat is likely group controller with no deputy.

name: Sharaf Group
why: Retail plus logistics plus hospitality in one group — unusually close to his composite experience.
watch: Private and lean. The job is broad; the title may be smaller than the scope.

name: Jashanmal Group
why: Long-established retail and distribution; Indian-managed finance function.
watch: Modest scale means the controller seat and the CFO seat may be the same chair.

name: Azadea Group
why: Franchise multi-brand retail across the Levant and GCC — direct read on his Landmark brand-portfolio work.
watch: Lebanon-headquartered with GCC operations; group finance sits outside the UAE.

name: Rivoli Group
why: Watches and luxury retail distribution; Indian-managed finance.
watch: Niche and small. One seat, rarely open.

name: Spinneys
why: Recently listed grocer — listed reporting plus grocery gross-margin management, and a finance function being built out post-IPO.
watch: Post-IPO teams hire fast then freeze. Timing is the whole game.

name: Liwa Trading Enterprises
why: ADQ-linked multi-brand retailer. Abu Dhabi retail at real scale.
watch: Abu Dhabi base and a smaller finance team than the Dubai majors.

name: Emirates Fast Food Co
why: McDonald's UAE franchisee — unit economics and franchise fees, a clean read.
watch: Single-brand, single-market. Narrow.

name: Al Nabooda Automobiles
why: Automotive retail: inventory, floor-plan financing and dealer margin — adjacent to retail inventory work.
watch: Single sector, modest scale.

name: NMC Healthcare
why: Large private healthcare group rebuilding its finance function after restructuring — unusual appetite for controller hires.
watch: The restructuring history is the risk. Diligence the balance sheet before the interview, not after the offer.

name: Aster DM Healthcare
why: Indian-promoted healthcare group operating across the GCC and India; Indian CAs throughout finance leadership.
watch: Healthcare revenue cycle and insurance receivables are a specific technical gap.

name: Burjeel Holdings
why: ADX-listed healthcare with an expansion programme.
watch: Same revenue-cycle gap; listed process adds rounds.

name: Mediclinic Middle East
why: Large managed hospital estate with cluster finance.
watch: South-African parent reporting norms and a preference for healthcare-native finance.

name: Dubai Investments
why: Listed holding company across manufacturing, real estate and services — consolidation and segment reporting at the centre.
watch: Holding-company finance is reporting-heavy and FP&A-light. Check which half the seat is.

name: ADNOC Distribution
why: Listed fuel retailer with a convenience-store business — genuine retail FP&A inside an energy group.
watch: Abu Dhabi, Emiratisation-dense, and strong internal pipelines.

name: ENOC
why: Dubai government fuel retailer with a large retail network.
watch: Government-related entity hiring preferences and process length.

name: Dulsco Group
why: Services group with multi-contract P&L management.
watch: Services margin work rather than retail. Weak sector read.

name: Al-Futtaim Technologies
why: Distribution economics inside the Al-Futtaim house — a side door into the group he most resembles.
watch: Technology distribution is a different gross-margin shape. Use it as a route, not a destination.

name: Emirates NBD
why: Scale guarantees many finance seats, and a bank's FP&A function is large.
watch: Banking capital, IFRS 9 ECL and regulatory reporting are a different trade. He would be the weakest candidate in the room.

name: First Abu Dhabi Bank
why: Same scale argument.
watch: Same disqualifying technical gap, plus Abu Dhabi Emiratisation density.

name: Mashreq Bank
why: Large finance function with business-partnering seats.
watch: Same gap. Listed here for completeness, not as a target.

name: Majid Al Futtaim Retail
why: The Carrefour franchise entity specifically — grocery gross margin, supplier income and franchise fees, which is the densest retail-FP&A job in the region.
watch: Posted roles often sit at specialist rather than controller grade. Read the grade, not the title.

name: Al Ansari Exchange
why: Listed and Indian-CA-dense, with branch-network unit economics that behave like retail.
watch: Regulated money-services reporting is a specific gap.

name: Emaar Malls / Dubai Mall ops
why: Mall operations finance: tenant turnover rent and footfall-to-revenue analytics, which is retail FP&A from the landlord side.
watch: Sits inside Emaar's internal pipeline.

name: Agility / Alshaya logistics
why: Regional logistics with retail-adjacent contract P&Ls.
watch: Logistics-native competition.

name: Thumbay Group
why: Indian-promoted group spanning hospitals, education and retail pharmacy.
watch: Smaller scale; the controller seat is broad and lightly resourced.

name: Sunway Group
why: The closest Malaysian structural twin to Landmark: malls, hotels, hospitals and property under one listed group. If he stays in Malaysia, this is the first call.
watch: Listed Malaysian group: MIA membership expected, local-hire preference real, and the EP seat has to clear RM20,000 for Category I.

name: Berjaya Corporation
why: Starbucks Malaysia, hotels, property and retail — franchise plus owned retail, the exact mix he reports on now.
watch: Complex listed group structure and the same EP threshold arithmetic.

name: YTL Corporation
why: Large diversified listed group with hotels and property.
watch: Utilities and infrastructure dominate; the retail-adjacent seats are few.

name: Genting Malaysia
why: Resort and hospitality P&Ls at genuine scale with a large FP&A function.
watch: Gaming regulation and a strong internal ladder.

name: IOI Properties
why: Listed developer with malls and hotels.
watch: Development accounting gap plus EP arithmetic.

name: Sime Darby Property
why: Largest listed Malaysian developer by landbank.
watch: GLC-adjacent governance and strong local-hire preference.

name: SP Setia
why: Listed developer with international projects.
watch: Same.

name: Mah Sing Group
why: Listed developer, leaner finance function.
watch: Same, with fewer seats.

name: Gamuda
why: Large listed engineering and property group.
watch: Construction contract accounting under IFRS 15 is a distinct technical gap.

name: UEM Sunrise
why: Listed developer, Khazanah-linked.
watch: GLC hiring norms.

name: Eco World Development
why: Listed developer with a strong brand and a defined finance ladder.
watch: Same sector gap.

name: Tropicana Corporation
why: Listed developer with retail and hospitality assets.
watch: Smaller finance team.

name: Paramount Corporation
why: Listed group spanning property and education.
watch: Modest scale.

name: Hap Seng Consolidated
why: Large listed diversified group — consolidation and segment reporting at the centre, which is his daily work.
watch: Diversification means generalist finance; the retail read is partial.

name: Hong Leong Group
why: Very large private and listed group with many finance seats.
watch: Banking dominates the group's finance hiring.

name: Boustead Holdings
why: Listed diversified group.
watch: Restructuring history and GLC norms.

name: AEON Co (M)
why: Listed retailer operating department stores, supermarkets and malls — the purest Malaysian retail-FP&A seat on this list.
watch: Japanese parent reporting culture and a strong local-hire preference at controller grade.

name: Parkson Holdings
why: Listed multi-country department store operator — same-store sales, concession income and gross margin.
watch: Structurally challenged sector; finance roles here are cost-programme roles.

name: Mydin Mohamed Holdings
why: Large domestic grocery retailer.
watch: Domestic, family-owned, strong local-hire preference, and EP arithmetic is hardest here.

name: 99 Speed Mart
why: Recently listed, very large store network — unit economics at scale and a post-IPO finance build-out.
watch: Post-IPO teams hire in bursts. Domestic hiring preference is strong.

name: Mr DIY Group
why: Listed, high-growth, multi-country retail — gross margin and store-rollout FP&A, which is exactly the modelling he does.
watch: Lean, fast-moving finance function; expects immediate output.

name: Padini Holdings
why: Listed apparel retailer — closest sector match to his Landmark fashion brands.
watch: Small finance function; the controller seat may not exist separately.

name: Bonia Corporation
why: Listed multi-brand fashion retailer.
watch: Small scale.

name: Lotus's Malaysia
why: Large grocery chain with a mature finance function post-rebrand.
watch: Private-equity-owned: cost discipline and a preference for proven grocery finance.

name: QSR Brands
why: Largest QSR operator in Malaysia — franchise fees, unit economics and commissary cost accounting.
watch: Private and lean; strong local pipeline.

name: Berjaya Food
why: Listed Starbucks Malaysia operator — franchise economics in a listed wrapper.
watch: Small finance function.

name: Zus Coffee
why: Fast-scaling regional coffee chain building its finance function now — the clearest greenfield controller brief in Malaysian F&B.
watch: Early-stage: title inflation, resourcing risk, and equity rather than cash.

name: Texchem Resources
why: Listed group spanning industrial and restaurant operations.
watch: Industrial dominates.

name: FGV Holdings
why: Large listed agribusiness.
watch: Plantation and commodity accounting is a different trade; GLC norms.

name: Shangri-La Hotels Malaysia
why: Listed hotel operator — property-level and cluster controller seats.
watch: Hotel finance usually entered at property level.

name: Sunway Hotels & Resorts
why: Hotel arm of the group that is already his best Malaysian target.
watch: Apply to the group, not the subsidiary.

name: Malaysia Airports
why: Large listed operator with substantial retail concession income.
watch: GLC: local-hire preference is at its strongest here.

name: Capital A / AirAsia
why: Listed aviation group with a large and frequently restructured finance function.
watch: Financial distress history and aviation-specific accounting.

name: DKSH Malaysia
why: Swiss-parented distribution group — principal-vs-agent revenue judgement is the core technical question, and MNC pay bands can clear Category I.
watch: Distribution, not retail. And a matrixed regional reporting line.

name: Nestlé Malaysia
why: Listed FMCG with a large FP&A function and genuine career structure. MNC pay bands make the EP arithmetic work.
watch: FMCG trade-spend and standard costing differ from retail gross margin; strong internal pipeline.

name: Unilever Malaysia / GSC
why: Global shared-service and FP&A hub in KL — MNC bands, regional scope, and the seat exists by design.
watch: Shared-service FP&A can be process-heavy and distant from commercial decisions. Ask what the seat owns.

name: Shell Business Operations KL
why: Large KL finance hub with controller-grade seats and Category I pay bands.
watch: Energy-sector reporting and a process-centred remit.

name: BASF Asia-Pacific Service Centre
why: Regional finance hub in KL with real controller seats.
watch: Chemicals and shared-service process work; weak sector read.

name: Roche Services Asia Pacific (KL)
why: Regional finance hubs with MNC pay bands.
watch: Pharma shared services; narrow sector read.

name: Novartis KL finance hub
why: Regional finance hubs with MNC pay bands.
watch: Pharma shared services; narrow sector read.

name: Kerry Group / Kerry Logistics MY
why: Regional operations with multi-entity reporting.
watch: Logistics-native competition.

name: Standard Chartered GBS KL
why: Very large KL hub with many finance seats and Category I bands.
watch: Banking technical gap.
